questions.q: Choose the correct form: “Neither he nor I ____ to blame.”
questions.why: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'I'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “It is high time we ______ the old files.”
questions.why: 'It is high time' + subject + past tense (subjunctive). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive form: “I don’t like people laughing at me.”
opts: I don’t like being laughing at.
I don’t like being laughed at.
I don’t like be laughed at.
questions.why: After 'like' the passive gerund is 'being + past participle'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the part of speech of “yet” in: “It was raining, yet we went out.”
questions.why: It joins two clauses and shows contrast. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct word: “For ____ details, please contact the office.”
questions.why: 'Further' means additional; 'farther' refers to distance. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct conjunction: “It was not until midnight ____ the fever subsided.”
questions.why: Cleft structure: 'It was not until ... that'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “Government by a small group of people”
questions.why: Oligarchy is rule by a few persons. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “ostensible”:
questions.why: 'Ostensible' means seeming or outwardly stated, though perhaps not real. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct negative transformation: “Only a fool would say that.”
opts: Only not a fool would say that.
A fool would not say that.
Not a fool would say that.
None but a fool would say that.
questions.why: 'Only' = 'none but' (keeps the meaning). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to eat humble pie”:
opts: to apologise humbly and admit one's error
questions.why: The idiom means to accept humiliation after being proved wrong. GPSC-style practice item.
